 Judgment
Challenging judgment and award dated 14.06.2018 passed by MACT and IV Additional District Judge, Vijayapura (for short, 'Tribunal'), in MVC no.656/2015 this appeal is filed.

2. Shri Basavaraj R. Math, learned counsel for appellants submitted that this appeal was by claimants challenging finding of tribunal on negligence as well as for NC: 2023:KHC-K:7360 enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that on 18.07.2014 deceased Pandurang was riding motorcycle bearing Reg.no.MH-09/CX-8034 from Kavala Naka to Shiroli, when it dashed against Lorry bearing Reg.no.MH- 44/9822 parked by its driver on road without taking precautionary measures.
Due to accident Pandurang sustained grievous injuries and died during treatment.
Claiming compensation, petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act was filed against owner and insurer of lorry.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Despite service of notice, owner did not appear and was placed exparte.

Insurer filed objection,
not only denying negligence of lorry driver but also alleging sole negligence against motorcycle rider.
Violation of policy condition was also alleged.
4. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant no.1 and another witness as PWs.1 and 2 and got marked Ex.P1 to P11.
Respondents NC: 2023:KHC-K:7360 did not lead oral evidence but got marked copy of insurance policy as Ex.R1 with consent.
5. On consideration, tribunal held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver and also rider of motorcycle equally.
It assessed total compensation of Rs.11,41,000/- and held claimants entitled for 50% of same i.e. Rs.5,70,500/- from insurer.
6. It was submitted that admittedly accident occurred during night time.
Ex.P11-charge-sheet was filed only against lorry driver for various offences including Section 122 of M.V.Act.
This would give rise to presumption that lorry was parked on road without adequate precautionary measure.

It was also pointed out that as per Ex.P3-spot panchanama, width of road at accident spot was only 20 ft.
and parking of vehicle much less a heavy goods vehicle as lorry without precautionary measure such as indicators, blockade and signage would call for holding entire negligence against lorry driver.
For enhancement, it was submitted that deceased was 31 years of age, earning Rs.15,000/- per month from private service.
However, tribunal considered meager monthly income of Rs.6,000/-.
It was submitted that tribunal also erred in not adding future prospects and granting appropriate compensation under conventional heads.
On above grounds, sought for allowing appeal.
8. On other hand, Sri Subhash Mallapur, learned counsel for respondent no.2-insurer supported impugned award.

9. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award.
10.

From above submission, since claimants are in appeal challenging finding of tribunal on negligence as well as seeking for enhancement of compensation, points that would arise for consideration are :
"i) Whether finding of tribunal on negligence calls for interference ?
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7360 ii) Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?"
Point no.(i):

3 11.

entities.text: Kalpana And Ors vs Hanumant Trimbak Sudake And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To establish negligence on part of driver of lorry, claimants produced FIR, complaint, spot panchanama, inquest panchanama, IMV report and charge-sheet marked as Exs.P1 to P.3, P6, P9 to 11.

Ex.P1-FIR and Ex.P6-charge-sheet would indicate that complaint was lodged against driver of lorry and charge- sheet was filed only against him for offences punishable under Sections 304-A,
338, 427 read with Sections 122, 134(A)(B), 105, 229 read with Section 177 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Prosecution of lorry driver for offences under Sections 122 and 177 of M.V. Act would prima facie establish that lorry driver had parked lorry on road in negligent manner.
But it is settled law that charge sheet by itself cannot be said to establish negligence against driver of lorry.

Though regulation no.15 of Road Regulation 1989 does not totally prohibit parking of vehicles on road, there is bar only against parking vehicle NC: 2023:KHC-K:7360 without safety-precautionary measure.
Even if for sake of arguments if it be accepted that lorry was parked unsafely, same would not justify motorcyclist dashing against lorry.
There is no evidence to indicate that rider of motorcycle had attempted to stop vehicle and avoid collision.
Therefore, in peculiar facts and circumstances of this case, apportionment of contributory negligence against rider of motorcycle can be safely taken as 20% and 80% against driver of lorry.
Point no.(i) is answered in affirmative.
Point no.(ii):
12. Insofar as quantum of compensation, though claimants stated that deceased Pandurang was earning Rs.15,000/- per month from private service, same is not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, same has to be assessed notionally.
But notional income for year 2014 is Rs.7,500/-.
Therefore, same has to be considered.
13. As on date of accident deceased was 30 years of age, self-employed and claimants are wife, two children and mother i.e. four dependants.

As per ratio in case of NC: 2023:KHC-K:7360 National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others, claimants would be entitled for addition of 40% of income towards future prospects, deduction towards personal expenses to be '1/4th' and multiplier applicable will be '17'.

entities.text: NC: 2023:KHC-K:7360 National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, loss of dependency would be (Rs.7,500 + 40% - 1/4th) X 12 X 17)= Rs.16,06,500/-.
14.

Apart from above, claimant no.1 would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium, claimants no.2 & 3 for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of filial consortium and claimant no.4 towards loss of parental consortium of Rs.40,000/-.

They would also be entitled to Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.
Since more than three years have lapsed they would be entitled for addition of 10% (Rs.19,000/-) to award under conventional heads.
Thus, total compensation would be Rs.17,42,880/-.
Point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative.

15. Consequently, following :
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7360 ORDER Appeal is allowed in part, dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.2 - insurer of Lorry is set-aside.
Thus total compensation would be Rs.17,42,880/-.

Claimants would be entitled for 80% of same i.e. Rs.14,52,400/-, which shall carry interest at rate of 6% per annum Kalpana And Ors vs Hanumant Trimbak Sudake And Anr on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129134142/
4 from date of petition till deposit, from respondents no.1 & 2 jointly and severally.
Insurer is directed to deposit compensation within six seeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
Directions issued by tribunal regarding apportionment, deposit and release shall apply as per tribunal award.
